evidence.estrutura: Mott organized through voluntary associations and reform networks, suggesting decentralized civic organization without a constitutional federal doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Abolitionism and Seneca Falls women’s-rights work strongly support equal citizenship and expanded democratic participation.
evidence.poder: Antislavery activism directly opposed extreme coercion and legal domination, placing her strongly on liberty and equal-rights principles.
evidence.imigracao: Her universalist Quaker abolitionism supports human equality and inclusion, though immigration law was not a major issue.
evidence.diplomacia: Quaker pacifism strongly supports nonviolence and diplomatic settlement.
evidence.intervencao: Pacifist principles and opposition to coercion favor non-intervention and peaceful reform.
evidence.economia: Her reform work challenged slavery and supported women’s economic/legal rights but did not define a socialist ownership system; moderate market reform.
evidence.controle: Voluntary reform and legal equality imply moderate/low centralized economic control.
evidence.comercio: Abolitionist boycotts show moral use of commerce but not a general tariff doctrine; moderately open/internationalist.
evidence.religiao: Quaker ministry was central to her life, making her personally religious while her egalitarian faith opposed clerical hierarchy and theocracy.
evidence.moral: Abolition and women’s equality strongly support progressive egalitarian social values.
